findings.problem: The replacement other-pool create-batch negative ('batch creation rejects only the wrong requested pool in an otherwise valid request') sends CASE 17 with poolId 00000000-0000-7000-8000-000020000002. Seed 20-fixtures-rait.sql:66 makes CASE 17 a 'cetran' case, and seed line 3 makes pool 20000002 'JARI-AM' with instance 'jari'. So the 404 comes from the `qp.instance=${c}.instance` term of poolCaseSql (rait-case-scope.service.ts:853-854). It does not come from the exact-routing disjunction (active case_pool_scope / active assignment / LOTE_ACEITO batch for that exact pool). The deleted test this replaces ('…another same-unit pool') and P4-02-S1-source-review-resolutions.md lines 37-41 ('Tests with a second same-unit pool establish isolation/negative controls … A unit shortcut cannot authorize another pool's case') require the same-unit, same-instance case. That case is still not shown for create-batch over HTTP. If poolCaseSql regressed to plain instance+unit inference, every create-batch test would still pass: the CASE 19/pool 20000002 positive at line 1035, this cross-instance negative, and its CETRAN positive. The runtime check itself (rait-worklist-command.service.ts:556-567, poolCaseSql per caseId before persist) is correct and is now reachable. Only the boundary proof is missing.
findings.recommendation: Add an HTTP+DB negative whose only defect is a different pool with the same unit and the same instance. Insert a second active 'jari' pool with the same unit_id as pool 20000002, and give RAIT_SECRETARY an ATIVO 'secretaria' membership in it. CASE 19 has no routing link to that pool, and its active assignment at seed line 135 stays bound to 20000002. POST /batches with that pool and caseIds [CASE 19] must return 404 with no data, an unchanged effects() result and unchanged inf.rait_batch/rait_batch_item rows. The same payload with poolId 20000002 must return 201. Keep the existing cross-instance test as an additional control.
